why: Commits 1 and 2 are mechanical: an add-only column, then 'main' added at 31 listed call sites (the count of 33 checks out) and held by a scan and the type check. Commit 3 is judgement the brief hands to '[an executor]': writing at least 25 fixed cases whose code checks really separate a good answer from a bad one for tone, summaries, memory, categories and highlight words, exporting each job's private prompt and parser without changing behaviour, and building a new eval runner, button and replay. Commit 4 depends on a real run by a person and on the owner adding price rows, and moving jobs changes which model, and so which price, every store's AI allowance is charged at.
harm_if_wrong: Weak cases that pass a quick model on jobs it does badly would move support tone, summaries or the AI manager's memory onto a weaker model for every store with no test noticing, and a quick model with no price row would stop counting toward stores' AI allowances.
make_it_cheaper: Write the 25 small-job cases and their expected parsed answers into the brief (or into a fixture file a stronger model prepares), and add the migration that widens ai_eval_runs' suite check to commit 1; then commit 3 is cheap-then-review and only commit 4 needs a person.
brief_problems: commerce.ai_eval_runs has check ai_eval_runs_suite: suite in ('agents') (src/db/schema.ts line ~16841), so storing a run with suite 'small_jobs' is refused; commit 3 needs a migration the brief does not mention.
Commit 3 is addressed to '[an executor]' and stop_if says to stop 'if you are [an executor] and reach commit 3'; the brief contradicts itself about who does it.

Commit 2 re-tags the memory pass as 'assistant_memory', which changes what step 1.19's per-feature figures and any feature-based limits count; the brief calls this intended but checks nothing that reads the feature.
